back: Storage, processing and software delivered over the internet on demand from a provider's servers.
Software as a Service: a finished application used over the internet, such as web email.
Platform as a Service: tools and servers on which customers build and run their own applications.
Infrastructure as a Service: virtual servers, storage and networks that the customer configures.
Public: shared by many customers. Private: used by one organisation. Hybrid: a combination of both.
Scalability, no hardware to buy, access from anywhere, automatic backup and updates.
Security and privacy of data held by a provider; dependence on a connection and on the provider; less control.
A copy held off-site survives loss of the building; protect it with a strong password and encryption; copying time depends on connection speed.
